spans.s: रोमकूप, i. e. रोमन्-, m. a pore of the skin.
+ गात्र रोमाञ्चित- + गात्र, adj., f. रा, with horripilation of the body, Pañc. 128, 21.
रोमगुच्छ, i. e. रोमन्-, n. a sort of whisk.
रोम, n. Water.

रोमन्, i. e. रुह् + मन्, n. The hair of the body, Pañc. iii. d. 186.
 --Comp.

रोमन्थ, probably a noun derived from रुज्, and compounded with मन्थ् + अ, m.
 1. Ruminating, Śāk. d. 39.
 2. Chewing,
Rājat. 5, 364

.
 --Cf. O.H.G. ita-ruchjan; A.S. roccettan; Lat. rūmen, ruminare (for rug-men), ructare; ἐρεύγομαι (old frequent.), ἐρυγγάνω, ὀρυγγάνω, etc.
रोमन्थाय, a denomin. derived from रोमन्थ with य, Ātm. To ruminate, Pāṇ. iii. 1, 15.
रोमवन्त्, i. e. रोमन् + वन्त्, adj., f. वती, Hairy, woolly.

रोमश, i. e. रोमन् + श,
 I. adj.
 1. Hairy,

. Woolly.
 II. m.
 1. A ram.
 2. A hog.
रोमाञ्च, i. e. रोमन्-अञ्च् + अ, m. Horripilation, considered as a sign of rapture, Pañc. ii. d. 175.

रोमाञ्चित, i. e. रोमाञ्च + इत, adj.
 1. Affected with horripilation, Utt.

Rāmac. 81, 4.
 2
. Enraptured, Pañc. 128, 21.
रोमलता, i. e. रोमन्-, f. a line of hair extending to the navel.
रोमविकार, i. e. रोमन्-, m. horripilation (cf. रोमाञ्च).
रोमहर्ष, i. e. रोमन्-, m. horripilation.

रोमहर्षण, i. e. रोमन्-,
 I. adj. causing the hair to stand erect, terrible,

.
 II. n. horripilation, caused by pleasure.
